name: Belarus

findings.summary: Infrastructure operator beCloud began commercial LTE Advanced service in Minsk with about 150 base stations, on Huawei-supplied equipment, open to all mobile operators; MTS subscribers connected first.

sources.note: confirms beCloud regional LTE rollout from Dec 2016; does not name the vendor

findings.analyst_inference: Vendor attribution rests on dev.by alone; the Onliner piece corroborates the beCloud network rollout but not Huawei as supplier, so not marked corroborated. Whether Huawei still supplies the expanded LTE/5G single network is unverified.

findings.summary: Under Decree No. 139 (1 April 2025) beCloud became sole 5G/LTE infrastructure operator for 2025-2034; MTS and Life launched commercial 5G in April 2026 in Minsk and four regional centres, each citing over 1,000 base stations.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Communications and Informatization of Belarus

findings.analyst_inference: Coded domestic because beCloud, a Belarusian company, operates the network; its RAN/core vendor is not named in either source. Tier 5 for commercial operation, though coverage so far is limited to five cities.

findings.summary: Russian vendor Irteya planned to start testing its own 5G base stations in Belarus in summer 2025; a Belarusian operator source said Huawei, Ericsson and Nokia are main suppliers, with Samsung and ZTE partly used.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third = Russia. The 1,000-station MTS figure in the article appears to refer to Russia's MTS, not MTS Belarus; not coded. Vendor-share statement is a single anonymous source. The article also reports Chinese vendors offering interest-free 10-year loans, unverified.

findings.summary: A1 Belarus tested 5G Standalone technology with ZTE in 2020; DCD noted it was unknown whether the planned single 5G network would use domestic or foreign vendors.
findings.analyst_inference: Trial only (tier 2). A1 Belarus is a subsidiary of Austria's A1 Telekom Austria Group per general knowledge, not verified here.

findings.reversal_of: AWS availability to new customers in Belarus
findings.summary: AWS stopped accepting new customers from Russia and Belarus in March 2022, per a DCD headline.

sources.note: headline and date read from the DCD Belarus tag page; article itself could not be fetched

findings.analyst_inference: Coded as a reversal of operational (tier 5) US cloud access; scope (new sign-ups only vs existing customers) not verified from article text.

findings.summary: HPE announced it would leave Russia and Belarus because of the war in Ukraine, per a DCD headline.

sources.note: headline and date read from the DCD Belarus tag page; article itself could not be fetched

findings.analyst_inference: HPE sells servers and compute hardware, so filed under silicon as the closest layer; size of HPE's prior Belarus business not known. Part of a wider 2022 exit of US vendors that also includes Ericsson stating it has no presence or customer engagements in Belarus.

findings.local_actor: Government of Belarus (national public safety monitoring system)
findings.summary: Synesis subsidiary 24x7 Panoptes won the 2018 tender to run Belarus's national public-safety monitoring system on its Kipod facial-recognition platform; 13,000 cameras planned by 2021, 2,000 announced in 2019, mostly Minsk.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded domestic: Synesis is a Belarus-based firm, though its prominent co-founder is Russian-born. Camera hardware vendor not named; whether cameras are Chinese-made is unverified. Synesis was later placed under EU sanctions (date not stated in source).

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Communications and Informatization of Belarus
findings.summary: Belarus's communications minister said the ministry is working with China's NDRC to create a China-SCO-Belarus AI application cooperation centre; no launch date given. Belarus is also building domestic compute using open-source LLMs as a base.

sources.publisher: Beshenkovichi District Executive Committee (Belarus state site)

findings.analyst_inference: Tiered S4: Belarusian state site relaying an official announcement. Statement of intent only. Same page says Belarus was invited into WAICO's founding group, consistent with the global-layer WAICO row.

findings.controller: National Academy of Sciences of Belarus; Russian Academy of Sciences
findings.local_actor: National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
findings.summary: Belarusian and Russian academies of sciences discussed plans to jointly develop an AI language model, described by the outlet as ideologically correct; planning stage only, no timeline.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: joint Belarus-Russia control (domestic plus third) with no stated split. Belsat tiered S4 as a Polish state-funded broadcaster.

facilities.null_reason: Great Stone park search returned only PRC/Belarusian state pages with no specific data-centre or AI-campus project; no large DC project since 2023 found in 10 searches

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced; search budget spent on other layers

research_gaps: Which vendor(s) supply RAN/core for beCloud's 2026 5G single network (Huawei, ZTE, Irteya or mixed), and was it financed by Chinese concessional loans?
Second independent source confirming Huawei as beCloud LTE supplier.
Did Irteya base stations enter commercial use in Belarus after the 2025 tests?
Camera hardware vendors in the Kipod/national public-safety system (Chinese-made or not), and EU sanction date for Synesis.
Any data-centre or AI compute project at Great Stone industrial park; ownership and status.
Full text of DCD AWS (Mar 2022) and HPE (Jun 2022) exit articles, blocked in this run; check Nokia and other Western vendor exits specific to Belarus.
Status of the China-SCO-Belarus AI centre and the Belarus-Russia academies language model; which open-source LLMs underpin Belarus's domestic compute.
